headline: High: Airbyte’s broad egress can leak business data into prompt/content workflows, while prompt collections can amplify unsafe downstream use.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and can move business data through APIs, but the profiles do not show a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge to awesome-prompts. awesome-prompts is a content-writing prompt collection, so the interaction is plausible mainly through manual copy-paste, which is a low-risk pathway.
conditions: IF an operator copies Airbyte-generated text into awesome-prompts workflows
IF a shared file or clipboard bridge is introduced between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of raw outputs into prompt libraries
Add a short human review step before reusing generated text
Use read-only exports instead of shared editable files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad egress, so it can transmit sensitive content outward. awesome-prompts has no declared network egress, but if Airbyte outputs are pasted into prompt content or shared files, business data can leak into downstream text artifacts. The pair lacks an explicit isolation mechanism, so the default risk is moderate.
conditions: IF business data from Airbyte is copied into prompt files or prompt logs
IF the pair shares a workspace or synced folder
mitigations: Store Airbyte outputs in a restricted folder
Avoid placing business data into prompt repositories
Redact sensitive fields before reuse
Separate credentials and data directories
Review any shared exports before publishing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte has API/network write capability, while awesome-prompts shows no network egress or write surface. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable resources, shared OAuth scopes, or filesystem write contention, so direct capability conflict appears limited.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or API
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state
mitigations: Keep write targets disjoint
Do not grant shared API credentials
Run one agent read-only where possible
Document ownership of each mutable resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce transformed business data that awesome-prompts may reuse as prompt material or examples. Because awesome-prompts is a prompt-writing repository and no verification workflow is shown, Airbyte output could be treated as authoritative content and propagated without checks. The pathway is plausible, but not directly documented.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is fed into prompt curation or publishing
IF awesome-prompts is used without a verification or fact-check step
mitigations: Require source attribution for reused content
Add a fact-check step before publishing prompts
Mark generated text as untrusted until reviewed
Keep raw pipeline output separate from curated prompts

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and can egress broadly, while awesome-prompts has no declared data classes or residency controls. The profiles do not show a specific regulated class like PHI or EU PII, so this is a compliance-gap risk rather than a confirmed breach. The other agent is not cited for residency because it exposes no relevant compliance surface.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Airbyte into prompt artifacts
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared outputs
mitigations: Classify data before routing it
Avoid storing regulated data in prompt repositories
Set explicit retention limits on exports
Review residency requirements before sharing outputs
